notes:
## Content and reading decisions

Section 17 announces a recapitulation of the indexed V objects and the introduction of V with a sequence of J indices. The body starts with an ordered set I, defines its closed subsets as downward-closed subsets, and describes closure under arbitrary intersections and unions. Formula (82) gives the downward closure of A. The next paragraph discusses the opposite-order topology; (83) gives the upward closure of B, followed by the statement that this is the smallest open subset for the lower topology containing B. The unfinished final paragraph compares local closedness with the identity J = bar J intersect tilde J.

The relationship among A, its complement, and the subsequent J prompted a rereading of the entire opening expression of the second paragraph. The ink has a triangular A and a separate bar above the second A: L = I minus bar A. The ensuing hooked J in “pour que J soit fermé” is retained, despite the change of letter. The inserted adjective is written ouverte, including its terminal e. Neither the letter mismatch nor the agreement is corrected from the mathematics. The first reader did not prove or disprove the final equivalence. Root subsequently performed the targeted check recorded below.

The source order is intersections quelconques followed by et par réunions; the heavily retraced intersections remains a narrow doubt, without reconstructing an independently cancelled predecessor. Inférieure is a live raised insertion; the underline belongs to the cancelled canonique. The annotation to (82) says can, without a dot. The visible quantifier abbreviation is tte. In the last paragraph the two-bar sign abbreviates même, and loc! has an upright and a separate low dot. The leader for inserted Pour does not cancel the capital Une.

## Doubts and sheet

The third V index in the heading is compatible with J but heavily retraced; it remains V with a doubtful J index. Other retained doubts are the cancelled ens., on a, Si, capital before celui, membership condition, and Donc, together with the overwritten intersections. Their uncertainty is local and does not extend to adjacent clear formulas. No explicit authorial question mark or date is present.

The author writes 41 at the head; the section is numbered 17 and the displayed formulas are (82) and (83). The thin bottom-left 88 is later foliation in another hand and is preserved as a margin entry. The sheet is handwritten text with insertions and cancellations, no genuine diagram or drawing. The page ends at “ou encore”.

## Actual mathematical check

Checked the final locally-closed characterization using only the topology defined on this leaf. Its closed sets are downward-closed, so bar J is the down-closure of J; tilde J is the up-closure and the least open set containing J. If J=F intersection U with F closed and U open, bar J is contained in F and tilde J in U, giving bar J intersection tilde J contained in J; the reverse inclusion always holds. Conversely bar J intersection tilde J is a closed set intersected with an open set. Thus the written equivalence is valid. This mathematical check does not regularize the different letters A and J in the earlier sentence or the written abbreviation loc!.

### Blind reading corrections

Both heading continuations are one point followed by one short rule. The retraced third V index now admits Sigma/J/Delta without forcing the notation. The dense stability word has a visible terminal rule and following comma; its interior remains doubtful. The isolated sign before Soit is also left uncertain between a section mark and canceled lettering. Tte, can without a stop, de I, the terminal e in inserted ouverte, and the written equals sign for même were confirmed. After celui de I the short form is i.e without a terminal stop. No order-theoretic statement was changed by these spelling and notation decisions.
